title: Google Maps could soon make it easy to clean up your list clutter
summary: With a single-tap control to hide or show your pins for saved places on the map.
body: Credit: Akshay Gangwar / Android Authority TL;DR Google is testing a new option to hide all your saved places from the map view with a single tap. This could be accomplished through a consolidated “All saved places” superlist that could combine all saved places under a single roof. Google is also testing an option to simplify how you discuss specific lists using Ask Maps. Google Maps has become an indispensable part of our commute, and countless mobile phone users rely on it frequently. Among the many nifty features it offers, Google Maps lets you save places of importance or interest, such as the ones you’d like to visit , and you can even compile these into a list. These saved places are cataloged on Google Maps’ You tab, and also show up in the actual map view when you’re scanning the nearby area. If you don’t want your saves crowding up the map, you can also hide them, but the option currently requires you to hide them per list. To make the process a bit easier, Google is now testing an option to hide all your saved places from the map view at once.

title: HONOR Robot Phone hands-on: I can’t believe it actually works this well!

body: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kCAdTV7M25c It’s one thing to be following along with the development of the latest smartphone in your favorite series — maybe like one of the new Pixel 11 models debuting today. Rumors may go back and forth on specs over the months leading up to launch, but even just going into it, you probably have a solid idea of the sort of device to expect. But then there are the phones that really attempt to do something all-new, and the path these take to market can prove a whole lot more interesting. For the better part of a year now, going all the way back to last October, HONOR has been teasing a smartphone with a camera unlike any other: the Robot Phone. Instead of a camera fixed in place to the back of the handset like you’ll see almost everywhere else, the Robot Phone’s camera is on the end of an articulated gimbal arm, like you may be familiar with from cameras like DJI’s Osmo Pocket series.

title: Verizon is so fed up with cable vandals, it’s putting a $25,000 bounty on them
summary: Verizon faced network outage related issues earlier this week due to acts of vandalism.
body: TL;DR Verizon will give away $25,000 to anyone who provides information leading to the arrest of vandals who damaged the carrier’s network infrastructure. This follows widespread incidents of vandalism and theft in the recent past, which led to a service outage earlier this week. More than half of the reported incidents come from California and Texas, according to recent data. Earlier this week, Verizon confirmed that vandalism of fiber cables caused widespread disruptions to mobile and internet services across parts of Southern California and Los Angeles. While the carrier said at the time that law enforcement was brought in to investigate these incidents, it is now seeking the community’s help to identify the vandals. In a blog post , Verizon says it will offer a $25,000 reward to people who provide information about the vandals, provided it leads to an arrest and conviction. As the carrier points out, such disruptions can lead to devastating outcomes for sectors that rely on continuous access to mobile/internet services, such as healthcare and emergency response services.

title: This shocking Zoom bug allowed silent device takeovers on Android and iOS
summary: A zero-click bug allowed attackers to silently take control during live Zoom calls.
body: TL;DR A Zoom annotation flaw could let a malicious participant remotely take over another person’s device without any interaction. Researchers found and exploited the bug using publicly available AI models in fewer than 20 prompts. Zoom has patched the flaws, so updating the Zoom app is the most important thing you can do. Over the past few months, we have watched frontier AI models rapidly alter the cybersecurity landscape — from AI models breaking technical barriers to mounting regulatory scrutiny over weaponized AI capabilities . Now, a newly disclosed Zoom flaw shows just how serious that can become. Researchers used undisclosed publicly available AI models to uncover a vulnerability that could have allowed someone on a Zoom call to take control of another participant’s device. The flaw affected Zoom clients on Windows, macOS, Linux, iOS, and Android. Worse, the attack required no click, download, or other action from the victim. Simply being in the same meeting could be enough.

title: Google Photos’ new Moods feature turns your existing images into retro film frames
summary: Gosh, I feel old!
body: Credit: Shimul Sood / Android Authority TL;DR Google is starting to roll out a new editing feature, called Moods, in Google Photos. These presets add AI-powered color edits to your existing images, with several options for a retro vibe. Moods are said to be available for users globally and across both Android and iOS soon. Google Photos has plenty of AI-powered features , and many of them are devoted to making your photos and videos stand out through automated edits . Google is now adding another feature to this list, and it adds a classic mood to your photos with a single tap. Back in June, we saw the first reference to a new “Moods” feature that appears on the Create tab in Google Photos. As with other features placed under the umbrella of Photos’ Create tab, Moods appears to use AI for quick color edits to your photos, including a range of filters with a retro vibe. The feature’s icon resembles an analog camera film, suggesting it leans on film-style aesthetics that now seem to be gaining popularity as part of the modern luddite movement on TikTok and other social media platforms. You can also get a digicam vibe with filters inspired by the 2000s.

title: Google Sheets makes it less of a headache to import Excel files
summary: It also preserves formatting and structural data.
body: TL;DR Google Sheets can now preserve formatting and structural information while importing Excel files. Sheets now imports Excel worksheets as “Sheets tables.” It also keeps pivot tables intact, rather than converting them into static grids. Google has been steadily adding new features and improvements to Sheets, most recently offering Gemini integration and the ability to import 3D graphs from Excel sheets. Now, the web app is gaining even more improvements aimed at users importing Excel files into Google Sheets. Google announced in a blog post that Sheets is gaining two key improvements. First, when users import an Excel file into Sheets, its tables will be added as Sheets tables. This ensures that structural and formatting information remains intact and that Excel tables stay properly formatted when opened in Google Sheets.

title: Google Home’s rogue smart light problem should now be fixed
summary: Google appears to have acted fast to ensure the haunted-house phase didn't last long.
body: Credit: Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority TL;DR Google says it has fixed an issue that caused some smart lights to turn on without user input. The bug had been affecting Google Home users on iOS and involved lights from several different brands. Google hasn’t explained what caused the problem, but the original Reddit poster says their setup is back to normal. Google Home users had a slightly haunted-house problem on their hands earlier, with smart lights switching on by themselves without being asked. The good news is that Google now says the issue has been fixed. We reported on the bug this morning after users on Reddit described their connected lights turning on when they opened the Google Home app on iOS. In some cases, switching the lights back off didn’t help, as they would turn themselves on again seconds later. Reports involved lights from several brands, including Govee, Philips Hue, and Tapo, while the issue appeared to be limited to the iOS app.

title: Waze’s police alerts are MIA for some
summary: Police warnings aren’t always reaching drivers.
body: TL;DR Waze users are reporting missing police alerts, with some saying their reports earn points but never appear on the map or reach other drivers. Some warnings are also arriving too late, with users reporting speed-camera and police alerts just seconds — or even feet — before the hazard. Waze has separately acknowledged an Android back-button bug following a recent update. Waze ’s police alerts seem a little off right now. The Google-owned navigation app isn’t outright broken for all, but the issues that users are reporting aren’t entirely isolated either. Within the last week, disgruntled Waze users have taken to Reddit and the Google support forum to raise the alarm about issues with police reporting , disappearing alerts, and reports that don’t reach other drivers . Waze’s whole appeal is its community-first approach. Waze relies on its users to feed data into the app as they drive. See a crash? Quickly report it. Spot a hidden police cruiser? You can report it hands-free with your voice. However, as soon as that community-driven reporting approach starts acting up, the app’s whole appeal begins to fall apart.

Samsung DeX is a useful utility that has been around for nearly a decade, letting you turn your Galaxy smartphone into a desktop for the big screen. While this has been its core purpose, there’s no denying that some users, especially those with foldables like one of the Galaxy Z Fold devices , may also enjoy a desktop-like experience directly on their phones. A developer has devised a solution to this with an app that runs DeX locally on Galaxy foldables. title: Here’s why Google Messages has disabled its ‘Clear data’ button

body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Recent Google Messages beta builds (v20260731 beta onward) have disabled the Android system-level “Clear data” button. This is not a bug, as the accompanying Manifest declarations point to a new, unfinished “ManageSpaceActivity” that will likely be used for selective data management and cleanup within the Messages app. Until Google activates the feature, uninstalling updates or rolling back to a stable release are the only ways to completely wipe app data. The Google Messages beta build is a great way to try out upcoming features for the messaging app (as long as the server-side flags align with your preferences), ranging from revamped context menus to UI overhauls. However, if you’ve recently jumped into your phone’s system settings to free up storage from the app, you might have noticed something strange. Recent Google Messages beta releases no longer allow users to clear app data directly from the Android system settings page, leaving the “Clear data” option grayed out. YouTube is also expanding access to Premium Lite subscriptions. Everybody hates YouTube ads , right? For all the time you may spend grumbling about them, trying to block them , or complaining about how much it costs to eliminate them , it can be easy to forget that these ads are what make it possible for your favorite creators to support themselves and continue to produce the videos you love. title: Google is making it harder to build custom ROMs for Pixel phones
summary: Getting Pixel kernel source code is apparently no longer as simple as grabbing it from a public Git repository.
body: TL;DR Google reportedly replaced automatic code updates for Pixel hardware with a manual Google Forms request system. Developers report waiting weeks for Google Drive links instead of receiving instant code downloads. The upcoming GrapheneOS-powered Motorola phones are built specifically to avoid this exact problem. Unlike some of the best Android phones on the market, Google Pixels have traditionally given developers a clean, transparent canvas to inspect software, test early builds, and run alternative operating systems like GrapheneOS. However, a quiet shift in how Google handles Pixel source code is reportedly threatening that open reputation, and it could soon impact anyone using custom software on their phone. According to GrapheneOS on X , Google has apparently replaced public, instant code downloads for Pixel phone drivers with a manual request form. Instead of publishing code directly to open developer platforms where anyone can grab it, Google now requires developers to fill out a Google Form and wait for someone to send them a Google Drive link.

title: Anker SOLIX says most portable power stations waste up to 30% of their stored energy
summary: The company is publishing efficiency data it says the rest of the industry doesn't share.
body: Anker SOLIX has called out an entire industry over how it measures battery efficiency, and it’s using its own product to make the point. The company has published discharge efficiency data for its S Series portable power stations across a range of real-world loads, something it says makes it the first portable power brand to disclose this level of detail. Anker has also shared its testing methodology alongside the results. The issue, according to Anker, is how efficiency gets advertised in the first place. Most portable power brands quote a single efficiency figure, typically between 89 and 92%, measured near full load under ideal conditions. But that’s rarely how these devices actually get used. During a real outage, you’re more likely running a fridge, a CPAP machine, a router, and some lights, all of which draw under 300W, well below 15% of a typical 2,000W unit’s rated output. Anker says efficiency at those lighter loads commonly drops to 70 to 80%, meaning a meaningful chunk of stored energy never makes it to your devices.

title: Gemini is spooking Google Maps’ users by chiming in on chats uninvited

A growing number of Android/Pixel users are reporting that Gemini on their phones has suddenly started chiming in and replying to ambient, everyday conversations completely out of nowhere, even when the standard hotword detection for voice assistant settings was supposedly turned off. Reddit user Flat_Marsupial_4249 was spooked by Gemini on their Pixel 9a suddenly interjecting in a private conversation between them and their friend during a drive. What’s more, the comment was contextually relevant rather than a generic search result, indicating that the AI assistant had been listening all along, adding to the creepiness.

title: YouTube is auto-launching Shorts, and users aren’t happy

body: Credit: Joe Hindy / Android Authority TL;DR YouTube is increasing its push for Shorts by auto-launching them when people start the app. The behavior appears erratic, and not everyone is experiencing it — yet. YouTube hasn’t confirmed whether this is an experiment, an intended feature, or a bug. YouTube has a tendency to push Shorts in as many different ways as it can. You’d often find the top three, sometimes four, rows on your YouTube home page dedicated to Shorts. Sometimes, Shorts show up as recommendations under long-form videos instead of comments. Similar experiments don’t stop at YouTube, but there’s a recent one that pushes vertical content and particularly seems to annoy many users. Several posts across Reddit highlight how launching YouTube sometimes opens Shorts without a warning. That’s usually the case when you might have shut the app on a Shorts screen, but some people say that it persists even when the app has been closed on another page. Some even say YouTube opens Shorts on startup, even when they don’t watch vertical videos at all.
